coverage: 130 ordinary source corrections do not silently remove the oldest retained original; zero expiry policy preserves all history.
Preview leaves payloads and metadata intents unchanged; apply removes eligible archive payloads and retains immutable prepared intents.
Active Markdown/recap literal revisions protect originals. Combined retirement/expiry protects its own newly issued evidence references until response publication.
Corrupt originals, linked active sources and detected captured-head changes preserve payloads and remain visible failures.
Cancellation after intent, expired deadlines, operation limits, 64-MiB capture, 4096-entry inventory and 2048-intent capacity preserve pending originals with explicit status.
Read-only host policy refuses destructive expiry; active source paths cannot be passed to the low-level archive unlink boundary.
Competing real processes expire/count one original once. Actual SIGKILL before/after unlink retains one intent and fresh local passes never count an absent archive again.
Real temporary-daemon API verifies preview/apply, exact intent metadata, strict age types, unchanged active source and no additional provider call.

Ten memory browser checks include a closed zero-default expiry option, fractional-age rejection before submission, a 320-pixel layout, confirmed/protected/uncertain counts and collapsed receipts without automatic resubmission.
The canonical lane retains prior publication/promotion/retirement/current-view, CLI/workflow/action/model, Go and browser recovery qualification.
limitations: Root-managed public Markdown/JSON heads and literal revision references are inventoried conservatively. External databases/workflow receipts/files require active memory pins; this is not universal cross-system retention/forgetting.

Expiry permanently removes eligible unreferenced original payloads. Metadata intents retain hashes, paths, sizes and policy; prepared is not proof of completed unlink. Absent originals never substitute current bytes.

Original age uses filesystem mtime, not event/publication time. Removing the last reference may make an already-old archive immediately eligible. Matching content elsewhere conservatively protects all matching archived copies.
The explicit native/API policy is disabled by zero. The existing periodic retention engine does not automatically select archive expiry. No live service configuration or data was changed.

Inventories/captured memory/operations/metadata intents are bounded. Expiry/consumed-promotion receipt compaction and active recap-head retention remain open; an exhausted cap preserves originals and reports incomplete.
Unlink/directory fsync and process-death checks do not qualify storage power loss, Windows runtime, forensic device/snapshot/backup erasure or aggregate system RAM.
The single resource run covers synthetic bounds and subprocess cases. It is not a production/model/MCU limit, latency SLO, VRAM or retrieval-quality measurement.
Portable C code is unchanged. Its assertion-enabled core test passed in the host lane; the separate core-only lane and MCU target execution were not repeated.

One initial browser test timed out on a blank workspace after reload. Focused repeats passed; root cause was not established and no product fix is claimed. The later full browser rerun is separate evidence, not a clean first-run claim.
